page: Microsoft Azure D4pds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance built on the ARM64 processor architecture running under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The configuration provides 4 dedicated vCPUs along with 16.0 GB of memory, yielding a 1:4 CPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware GPU acceleration is not present on this instance type.

For local disk operations, the D4pds_v7 bundles a 236 GB local NVMe solid-state drive and maintains compatibility with Premium Storage. The integrated NVMe drive supplies fast, direct-attached transient storage for temporary data, swap space, or caching without incurring network storage latency. The instance does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The use of dedicated ARM64 cores provides high computational density and power efficiency for general computing tasks, offering favorable cost efficiency compared to traditional x86 alternatives. A key tradeoff is the requirement for arm64-compatible binaries and container images. This instance is suited for multi-tier web applications, microservices, continuous integration runners, and lightweight databases that utilize fast local cache.
description: Microsoft Azure D4pds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an ARM64 processor and managed via Microsoft Hyper-V. The system features 4 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is absent with zero GPUs provisioned. Local storage is provided through a bundled 236 GB NVMe solid-state drive, alongside compatibility with Premium Storage for remote volumes. Because it utilizes the arm64 instruction set, workloads require compatible software builds, yielding architectural power efficiency and solid compute density for everyday tasks. Without default complimentary public IPv4 addressing, networking configurations require user-allocated routing or private connectivity. The instance is appropriate for standard business workloads including web servers, application backends, container hosting, and databases that benefit from high-speed local scratch space.
